comparison: Both strongly support the central finding that UNC-6/Netrin functions via both haptotaxis and chemotaxis. OpenEval R13 addresses claims C3-C7, C119-C120, C142 as well-supported by combined evidence. Peer R1 explicitly affirms this central finding with all reviewers agreeing it 'potentially resolves the controversial question' and provides 'compelling support.' High agreement on the main conclusion.

Both support the characterization of axon guidance trajectories and pausing behavior at vSLNC (claims C21-C32). OpenEval R1 cites time-lapse imaging and electron microscopy as strong evidence. Peer R2 accepts these descriptive observations without challenge, noting the discrete stepwise process. Complete agreement on anatomical characterization.

Both support UNC-40 receptor polarization findings. OpenEval R2 addresses claims C38-C50 including polarization (C43-C50), citing endogenous UNC-40::GFP tagging. Peer R3 affirms UNC-40 polarization on growth cone membrane facing direction of growth, with no concerns raised. Strong agreement on receptor polarization mechanism.

Partial overlap on UNC-6/UNC-40 mutant phenotypes. OpenEval R2 covers claims C38-C50 including mutant analysis and receptor polarization. Peer R1 addresses broader conclusions including some mutant phenotype claims (C38-C42, C50). Both support the findings but peer review focuses on higher-level conclusions while OpenEval provides detailed assessment of mutant data.

Both support findings on directional growth and stabilization (claims C51-C57). OpenEval R3 cites quantitative branching analysis and adult morphology data. Peer R1 includes these claims in broader support for dual mechanism conclusion. Agreement on UNC-6/UNC-40 effects on both directional growth and stabilization.

Perfect claim overlap (C58-C65) on SLT-1/UNC-6 genetic interaction. Both strongly support that SLT-1 affects axon emergence direction while UNC-6 controls subsequent guidance, with additive effects in double mutants. OpenEval cites time-lapse imaging and genetic interaction analysis. Peer review accepts SLT-1 works in parallel to UNC-6. Complete agreement.

Strong overlap on MADD-2 ubiquitination findings (claims C66-C77). OpenEval R5 supports unc-40(4KR) evidence for ubiquitination role in UNC-40 polarization. Peer R4 explicitly highlights MADD-2 separation of adhesion/stabilization from directional growth as 'remarkable' and 'well-supported.' Both agree on the functional separation demonstrated by MADD-2 analysis.

Both support MADD-2 functional separation (claims C78-C81). OpenEval R6 cites quantitative branching and stabilization data showing MADD-2 affects adhesion but not directional growth. Peer R4 emphasizes this as a key finding distinguishing MADD-2 from broader UNC-6 role. Strong agreement on separation of function.

Strong overlap on membrane-tethered UNC-6 rescue experiments (claims C87-C93). OpenEval R7 supports spatial specificity of rescue demonstrating contact-mediated signaling. Peer R7 describes these experiments as central, noting restoration of growth cone contacts and restriction to nerve cords. Both agree membrane-tethered UNC-6 demonstrates haptotaxis mechanism.

Partial overlap on membrane-tethered rescue supporting haptotaxis. OpenEval R7 addresses claims C87-C93 on local UNC-6 signaling sufficiency. Peer R1 includes some of these claims (C89, C92-C93) in broader support for dual mechanism conclusion. Agreement that rescue experiments support contact-mediated haptotaxis.

Both support that membrane-tethered UNC-6 cannot rescue directional branching (claims C94-C98). OpenEval R8 cites inability to rescue as evidence for distinct diffusible UNC-6 role in chemotaxis. Peer R1 includes these claims in support for separable mechanisms. Agreement on requirement for diffusible UNC-6 in directional guidance.

Both support partial rescue findings (claims C99-C101). OpenEval R9 notes haptotaxis supports some guidance but is insufficient for complete rescue. Peer R1 includes these claims in overall support for dual mechanism requirement. Agreement that both haptotaxis and chemotaxis are required.

Strong overlap on endogenous UNC-6 distribution imaging (claims C102-C106). OpenEval R10 supports UNC-6 enrichment at targets and along filopodia, noting shallow gradient. Peer R5 praises UNC-6::neon green visualization as a strength. Both support the imaging data, though OpenEval notes qualification about gradient detection.

Both support UNC-40-dependent UNC-6 recruitment findings (claims C108-C110). OpenEval R11 cites comparative imaging showing loss of filopodia-associated UNC-6 in unc-40 mutants. Peer R5 accepts UNC-6 localization data without challenge. Agreement on UNC-40 dependence of UNC-6 recruitment.

Both support dynamic UNC-6 behavior findings (claims C111-C116). OpenEval R12 cites high-resolution time-lapse imaging showing dynamic UNC-6 clustering. Peer R5 praises UNC-6 localization demonstration as a strength. Agreement on dynamic UNC-6 visualization and quantification.

Strong overlap on background/prior work claims (C1-C2, C8-C20, C33-C37, C82-C84, C117-C118). OpenEval R14 notes these represent established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer R8 accepts background claims as established framework for the study. Agreement that prior work is appropriately cited and provides necessary context.

Overlap on prior work providing mechanistic context (claims C122-C125, C127, C130, C136-C138, C140-C141). OpenEval R15 notes these citations support mechanistic interpretations. Peer R8 accepts background claims without challenge. Agreement that prior literature is appropriately integrated.

Both address speculative mechanistic proposals (claims C133-C135). OpenEval R16 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable hypotheses lacking direct validation, appropriately presented as speculation. Peer R9 supports these as inferences consistent with data, not challenged by reviewers. Both recognize speculative nature but peer review more accepting of model-building.

Minimal overlap on speculative claims. OpenEval R16 addresses C107, C121, C126, C133-C135 as speculative but reasonable. Peer R10 addresses C27, C73, C107 as supporting claims not challenged. Both accept these as appropriately qualified speculation.

Partial overlap on summary/integration claims (C131-C132). OpenEval R17 supports these as valid conclusions integrating multiple evidence lines. Peer R9 accepts mechanistic interpretations as consistent with data. Agreement that summary statements are well-supported by experimental evidence.

Minimal overlap on MADD-2 summary claims (C129, C139). OpenEval R17 supports these as integrating MADD-2 and unc-40(4KR) evidence. Peer R4 emphasizes MADD-2 findings as well-supported. Agreement on validity of MADD-2 conclusions.

Minimal overlap on UNC-40 polarization summary (C128). OpenEval R17 supports as integrating UNC-40::GFP imaging evidence. Peer R3 affirms UNC-40 polarization findings. Agreement on summary of polarization mechanism.
